why: All three checks pass, so the finding stands. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w29.md returns the sentence character-for-character on line 63, inside the 'Other wins' digest grid. It is a one-sentence <div>; there is no second sentence and nothing later on the page qualifies or reverses it. The page is a legitimate contract source: it is row 191 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv (the 174-page llms.txt snapshot). (2) CITED FILE CONFIRMS: packages/pi-agent-server/src/tools/search/create-search-tool.ts:61 is `name: 'web_search'` inside createSearchTool(provider, fallbackProvider = new DDGSearchProvider()); the whole 115-line file contains no counter, no budget and no env read - execute() clamps only `count` to 1-10 (line 70) and otherwise calls provider.search unconditionally. Registered unconditionally at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1394 in `webTools`. It is the right subsystem: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-tool-descriptor.ts:256 binds it to Claude's `WebSearch` name. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, one layer up and one down: grep -ra -F MAX_WEB_SEARCHES over packages/ apps/ = 0 hits outside the sweep's own docs; grep -ra for SEARCHES_PER / WEB_SEARCH_PER / webSearchLimit / searchBudget = 0; the fork's own renamed-knob convention (NESSY_MAX_*) has exactly one member, NESSY_MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES, so the cap does not exist under a Nessy spelling either. Nothing upstream absorbs it: pi-agent.ts's only per-tool counter is lastAssistantToolCallCount (:662, :2633, :3876), a per-assistant-message count used to suppress a PreToolUse defer, not a session budget; DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG (harness-manifest.ts:103-111) carries concurrency/depth/maxParallelTasks/maxAgents/tokenBudget and no search budget; the near-miss same-name symbols are in unrelated subsystems (MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS in child-session-service.ts:44 and useSessionSearch.ts:18 cap session-transcript search results; maxMatchesPerSession in server-core/src/services/search.ts:194 is transcript search too; hook_loop_cap in session-lifecycle.ts:59 caps hook recursion). Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 touches web search or session caps, and the file has no 'web search' hit at all. Not a deliberate product difference: this is neither a subscription flow, a gateway concern, nor a rename - it is a missing runaway-loop backstop.
correctedState: The finding is correct, with two scope refinements. (a) Name the subsystem: the uncapped tool is the Pi harness's `web_search` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/tools/search/create-search-tool.ts:56-114, registered at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1394), which harness-tool-descriptor.ts:256 binds to Claude's `WebSearch`. Under the opt-in Claude Agent SDK backend (NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE, off by default) the SDK's own WebSearch carries whatever caps Anthropic ships, so the exposure is Pi-specific. No session-wide web-search counter, default, or env knob exists anywhere in packages/ or apps/, under either the CLAUDE_CODE_ or the NESSY_ spelling. (b) The doc sentence's subagent half is partially, and only partially, covered - worth recording because it is the closest thing to an upstream absorber and it does not absorb this: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/workflow-tool.ts:37-40 has DEFAULT_MAX_AGENTS = 1000 commented 'T1: Claude-Code-class runaway backstop', plus a depth limit (spawner.ts:519) and a concurrency semaphore (spawner.ts:204). Those are workflow-scoped and depth/parallelism-scoped, not a session-wide spawn count, and 1000 is not 200; neither reaches web_search at all.
